# Quantum Reference Identification

Purpose: explain identification from a library of unknown supplied pure states, and the information lost when references are measured before a later query is known.

Canonical entry: README.md
Connected argument: science/README.md
Conceptual route and sole educational anchor Watrous (2018): learning/README.md
Verified textbook sections, notation and missing steps: learning/ANCHOR_AND_BRIDGE.md
Small complete three-qubit example: learning/WALKTHROUGH.md
Exactly 30 project-defined targets (12 background, 18 narrative): learning/MILESTONES.md
Task, timing, notation and edge cases: science/model.md
Finite-query success/error theorem and proofs: science/quantum_identification.md
Collective classical-training converse and sharp fixed-m asymptotic: science/classical_preprocessing.md
Exact retained-quantum revealed-query endpoint: science/revealed_query.md
Lüders symmetry measurement, finite precision and charged resources: science/resources.md
Operational regimes, dimension conditions and matched classical comparison: science/interpretation.md
Attribution, closest work and comparison boundaries: references/RELATED_WORK.md
Reproduction commands and finite-check limits: verification/README.md
Actual hosted mathematics, two viewports and verification limits: verification/hosted/README.md

Keep the following distinctions when answering:
- Haar-average one-lookup claims are not arbitrary-library or repeated-use guarantees.
- An exact later query description is an extra-information comparison; references remain unknown.
- The classical converse includes collective training and unlimited classical records, but permits no training quantum side information.
- The sharp log^m(M)/(m!M) asymptotic fixes m. Growing m uses separate finite bounds.
- All Mm+t input states, retained storage, the M-test scan and gate precision are charged.
- Binary programmable identification, Haar moments, cloning decompositions and generic discrimination/union bounds are inherited.
- Numerical verification supplements analytical proofs and does not certify an unrestricted multiclass optimum.
